To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have developed the first Micromegas readout with 2.5 mm pixel pitch and 3 mm drift gap, and have operated it in a 35 cm drift length, 28 cm diameter TPC filled with a Xenon gas mixture.

the NEXT-MM prototype, the largest micromegas readout TPC operated in xenon ever constructed and the largest single wafer micromegas detector, has demonstrated the ability to reconstruct extended electron tracks, in particular those produced by gammas of 29 keV.

we have demonstrated the feasibility of a TPC with Micromegas readout for a large mass of Xenon gas and we have demonstrated that a TPC readout can be used to detect the ionization signal from a 20 cm electron track in Xenon gas, with a resolution of 12% at 29keV.

the development of the NEXT technology for the detection of rare events in the field of particle astrophysics, in particular for the detection of neutrinoless double beta decay of 136Xe, a process that would provide evidence of physics beyond the standard model of elementary particles.
